questions.question: Differentiate between normal and anomalous Zeeman effects in terms of cause, splitting pattern, and examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Normal Zeeman Effect: The splitting of the energy levels or spectral lines of
  • a substance placed in a magnetic field is called the Zeeman effect. In certain
  • cases, the line is split into three lines called the normal Zeeman effect.
  • Caused only by orbital angular momentum of the electron, the Spin of the
  • electron is not considered.
  • Interaction between the magnetic field and orbital angular momentum only.
  • Spectral line splits into three components- one (πcomponent) two (𝜎
  • components) Occurs when S = 0
  • Eg: 61D2→51P1 line of cadmium (Any similar example)
  • Anomalous Zeeman Effect: The phenomenon of splitting of spectral lines of
  • atoms having non-zero angular momentum in the presence of a magnetic field
  • is often more complex than the three lines observed in the normal Zeeman
  • effect.
  • It is caused by both orbital and spin magnetic moments and it results in the
  • interaction between the magnetic field and total angular momentum (J = L +
  • S) Spectral lines splits into more than 3 components
  • Occurs when S≠0
  • Eg; 2p3/2→2s1/2 line of sodium (Any similar example)
  • Explanation
  • with any one
  • example – 2.5

questions.question: Plot the rotational energy levels and allowed transitions for a rigid diatomic molecule up to the rotational quantum number 3. Give the nature of the spectra if an isotope of higher mass is replaced one atom in the molecule.
questions.solution_html:
• Transitions between rotational levels within a given vibrational level give the
  • pure rotational spectra in the far infrared or microwave region.
  • Transition between vibrational levels within the same electronic state

  • Caused only by orbital angular momentum of the electron, the Spin of the
  • electron is not considered.
  • Interaction between the magnetic field and orbital angular momentum only.

  • atoms having non-zero angular momentum in the presence of a magnetic field
  • is often more complex than the three lines observed in the normal Zeeman
  • effect.

  • interaction between the magnetic field and total angular momentum (J = L +
  • S) Spectral lines splits into more than 3 components
